summary: Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who taught Kuntala Bhattacharya. He has held posts at the University of Calcutta as a professor (attested 2009) and at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture.
Prabhasa Dharma Cheney (1931–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kyozan Joshu Sasaki in 1967 and Seikō Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1898–1956) was an Indologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Krishnagar Government College, Calcutta, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi, later holding posts at Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.

Pradyot Kumar Mukhopadhyay (born 1938) works in philosophy and Indology. He was a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research around 2007–2010.

Prafulla Chandra Ray (1861–1944) studied at Vidyasagar College, Presidency College, Chennai, Calcutta, and Edinburgh. Active in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held posts at Presidency College, Chennai, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta.

Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Patna and Visva-Bharati. He held posts at Visva-Bharati, Ravenshaw College, Utkal University, Gangadhar Meher University as principal, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Georgetown and Mumbai. He served at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, University of Chicago, and Harvard University as George P. Bickford Professor (1980–2004).
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD at the University of Mysore (attested 2014).

Pratap Chandra Chunder (1919–2008) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Hindu School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, where he studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi around 1940–1942.
Pratap Kumar Penumala is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. In 2010, he was attested as a professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a visiting professor at Colorado College.

Pratapaditya Pal (born 1935) specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Tibetology, earning degrees at Calcutta and Cambridge. He held curatorial and leadership posts at the Boston MFA, LACMA, the Art Institute of Chicago, and Norton Simon Museum.

Prayudh Payutto (born 1938) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He earned his bachelor's degree and served as associate dean (c. 1964–1973) at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, and was named Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark (1908–1980) worked in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics, and served in the Office of Strategic Services (c. 1944–1945).

Prods Oktor Skjærvø (born 1944) specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at Oslo and Mainz, later holding academic positions at Mainz, Columbia University, and Harvard University as Aga Khan Professor (c. 1991–2015).

Pulinbihari Chakravarti was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society, attested in 1951.

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat (1894–1991) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Mumbai and Harvard. He held academic posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi, where he held the chair for Buddhist studies.

Purushottama Bilimoria specializes in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, earning a PhD at La Trobe under Shivesh Thakur. He held posts at Deakin University, the University of Melbourne, and visiting professorships at Columbia and Stony Brook.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon (1891–1973) was active in Indology and other fields. He served as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and as president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at King's College London in 2014 and was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow there in 2017.

Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, he has been a fellow at All Souls College and held posts at Oxford and Eötvös Loránd University.
